Class GTNetMaintenanceWindow

java.lang.Object
grafiosch.entities.BaseID<Integer>
grafiosch.entities.GTNetMaintenanceWindow
@Entity public class GTNetMaintenanceWindow extends BaseID<Integer>
One announced maintenance window of a remote GTNet instance.

A row is written when a GT_NET_MAINTENANCE_ALL_C announcement of that remote is received. A peer may announce several windows, so this is a list per remote rather than a pair of columns on GTNet. The window is never turned into a persisted server state: every place that would contact the peer asks instead whether the current time falls into one of its windows. That way the state can be neither late nor stale, which it would be if a background job had to flip it — GNetFutureMessageDeliveryTask runs every five hours and could not open or close a window of a few minutes on time.

The row belongs to the announcement it came from. A GT_NET_MAINTENANCE_CANCEL_ALL_C referencing that announcement deletes its windows again, and the foreign keys to gt_net and gt_net_message both cascade on delete, so removing the peer or its message leaves nothing behind.

No ExportDefinition and no entity limit. Like every other gt_net* table this is instance-wide administrative data owned by no tenant and no user, so it is absent from "export my data" and from the deletion of an account by design. It is likewise unbounded on purpose: rows are written only by MaintenanceAnnouncementHandler while processing an authenticated peer message, never through a user-reachable write endpoint, and the unique key over the peer and the two window bounds makes a re-delivered announcement an upsert rather than a new row.
